events.text: Your first years above the clouds, the System is quiet. Then it speaks: "Up here everything is essence. The air. The light. Them." On a jade bridge a tall immortal in grey robes stops you, a ledger in one hand, a bronze measuring cup in the other. {npc}, Inspector of the Granary of Heaven. "Essence rises from the world below," {he} says. "Some of it, my ledger says, went into you."

effects.log: You let {npc} look. {He} holds the little cup to the dark behind your eyes, frowns, and writes: "Hungry. Honest about it." It is the kindest thing an inspector ever wrote.

choices.text: Say you have never devoured anything

effects.log: {npc} turns the cup over. A thread of light runs out of it, the colour of your last meal. {He} writes something down and does not tell you what.

choices.text: Ask what the System is, to Heaven

effects.log: "A shard," says {npc}. "Of something that ate the first light, before Heaven and Earth were two. The Granary has been collecting the pieces for a long time."

events.text: {npc}, an Inspector of the Granary of Heaven, stops you on a jade bridge and reads the ledger twice. "There is an entry here," {he} says slowly, "for a soul that fed the Maw the whole sky once, in another life. The hand is mine. I do not remember writing it." Inside you the System goes very still, like an animal that has been recognised.

effects.log: "Then the ledger was right to keep you," says {npc}, and for the first time an inspector of the Granary smiles at you.

choices.text: Say nothing, and listen to the System

effects.log: The System says one word, very quietly: "Again." It is not hungry when it says it. It sounds almost like hope.

events.text: The System finds the stars. "Look up," it says, thick and slow. "Every one of them is a meal nobody is eating." That night {npc} finds you at the edge of the isle with your face turned to the sky. "The Granary keeps that light for the world below," {he} says. "Every star you eat is a harvest that fails somewhere down there."

choices.text: Promise to eat only what is given freely

effects.log: You promise. The System sulks for a month. {npc} writes your promise into the ledger, which up here is the same thing as a vow.

choices.text: Say hunger is older than harvests

effects.log: "So am I," says {npc}, and closes the ledger. From then on {he} watches you the way granary cats watch the sacks.

events.text: An elder of an immortal sect falls in a duel on the isles, and the essence rises off the elder like mist off a lake. Before the System can move, {npc} is there with the bronze cup, catching it. "For the Granary," {he} says without looking at you. Inside your ribs the System makes a sound only you can hear.

effects.log: You hold the hunger back with both hands. {npc} fills the cup, seals it, and bows to you, very slightly, before {he} goes.
You are faster. The mist pours into you, clean and bright, and the cup comes up empty. {npc} looks at it for a long moment.

events.text: Your promise has a price. The hunger at the immortal scale gnaws harder than it ever did below, and the stars stay in the sky. {npc} brings you a jar from the Granary itself: the essence of a thousand harvests, given back by the fields below. "It is not much," {he} says. "It is what the world can spare."

effects.log: You eat it a grain at a time. It tastes of rain and threshing floors. For the first time in your life, the hunger says thank you.
"Let them keep it," you say. {npc} does not argue. Below, that autumn, the harvest is the best in a generation, and nobody knows why.

events.text: {npc} comes for you with the Granary's warrant, a scroll of light with one word on it, and two granary guards behind {him} carrying measuring cups the size of temple bells. "Give back the starlight," {he} says, "or I will measure it out of you."

ok.log: You win. The System drinks what rises from the fallen inspector's qi before you can stop it. {npc} gets up lighter and older, and does not come back for a long time.

fail.log: The bell-sized cups ring once and the hunger is drawn out of you in a long cold stream. You wake on the bridge, empty and furious.

effects.log: You open your mouth and let one thread of starlight go. It climbs back to its place. {npc} marks the ledger: "Partial. Promising."

events.text: Ding. The System has tasted enough starlight to understand something. "The sky," it says, and its voice is not thick any more, "is the bowl. It always was." It wants to stop being a mouth and become the bowl. {npc} stands beside you on the rim of the isle, the ledger shut. "If it does that," {he} says, "it will never be hungry again. Neither will you."

effects.log: The hunger spreads out from your golden core like ink in water until it is as wide as the night, and then, for the first time since the first light, it is full.

choices.text: Keep it a mouth, but a patient one

effects.log: "Not yet," you tell it. It grumbles, and grows anyway, slowly, into something that knows how to wait.

events.text: Even in the Divine Realm the System is hungry, and here the things it could eat are gods. It does not ask for one. It shows you the oldest bronze vessel in Heaven, a face with no body, and says: "That was me, before. I want to be whole without eating anything." {npc} has followed you even here, the ledger under one arm, and says nothing at all.

choices.text: Give it the sky to be its body

effects.log: You give it the sky. The bodiless face on the vessel closes its mouth, and in the Granary every ledger balances at once.

choices.text: Give it your own patience to be its body

effects.log: You give it your patience. It wears it like a robe, a little too large, and grows into it over the years.

events.text: The hunger is quiet now, a sky inside you with the stars put back. {npc} visits on the day of your old promise, with tea from the Granary. "One entry is left in my ledger with your name on it," {he} says. "A last meal: the System could eat the hunger itself, and you with it, and the sky would be full forever. I only tell you that it exists."

effects.log: "Not yet," you say. {npc} nods and pours the tea, and the two of you watch the stars, which are all still there.

choices.text: Ask what it would feel like

effects.log: "Like the end of a long winter," {npc} says. "Or so the ledger says. Nobody has ever come back to tell me."

events.text: The System has been patient for two whole years, which for it is a miracle. Tonight it says one thing more: "One meal is left. Me. And you with me. Then nothing above or below is ever hungry for us again." {npc}, who has stopped hunting you and started visiting, somehow hears it too, and goes pale.

effects.log: "Then I will keep visiting," says {npc}, "until you do." It is, from an inspector, a promise.
It waits. It is good at waiting now. That frightens you a little more than the hunger ever did.

events.text: Ding! Signed in: the Jade Stairs. Year after year of it. Then, one morning, the register adds a line it never added before: [New places available above the clouds.] An immortal in pale blue robes is waiting at the top of the stairs with a box of jade slips. "{npc}," {he} says, "Archivist of Heaven's Register. You sign in more than any god I keep. I came to see who you are."

effects.log: You open the register. {npc} turns the pages for a long time, year after year of your signatures. "Not one missed," {he} says, and sounds moved.

choices.text: Ask where the new places are

effects.log: {npc} points: a bell tower on a drifting isle, a ford of stepping stones across the Sky River. "Sign them all," {he} says. "Then we will talk about the last one."

events.text: {npc}, Archivist of Heaven's Register, meets you at the top of the Jade Stairs and does not say hello. {He} opens an old register to a page near the back. There is a signature on it in your own hand, from a life you do not remember, and beside it, in red: [Last Calendar: complete.] "You came back," {he} says. "Nobody comes back."

effects.log: You sign beside your old name. The two signatures look at each other across a whole life. Ding! The register is pleased.
"Punctual," says {npc}, and then, after a while: "Kind to archivists. Nobody is kind to archivists."

events.text: {npc} brings you a question from the register itself, written on a slip: [Faithful or far?] "Some sign the same ground ten thousand years," {he} explains, "and the ground becomes them. Some sign every ground once, and become the road. The Last Calendar is made of one or the other. The register would like to know which you are."

effects.log: "Faithful," you say. {npc} writes it down, and the Jade Stairs under your feet feel, for a moment, like a floor you have always had.
"Far," you say. {npc} smiles and writes it down. "Then the register will have to keep up with you," {he} says.

events.text: An immortal of the Jade Void Sect sneers at you on the Ford of the Sky River: a System that pays for showing up, how mortal. {npc} hears it, and quietly opens the register to the sneerer's own page. It is nearly empty. "Attendance," {he} says, "is the only thing Heaven cannot fake."

effects.log: You tell the immortal that ten thousand mornings are a cultivation too. The immortal has no answer. {npc} keeps the slip with your words on it.

choices.text: Invite the immortal to sign in with you

effects.log: To everyone's surprise the immortal does. The next year too. {npc} has to open a new page.

events.text: Faithful has a price. {npc} warns you: the register is closing pages above the clouds, and a ground nobody signs for a hundred years is struck from Heaven's maps. Your old ground below, the first road you ever signed, is on the list. To save it you must sign it from above, which the register says costs you a year.

effects.log: You kneel on the Jade Stairs and sign the old road below by name, letter by letter. It takes a year. The road stays on Heaven's maps.
The old road is struck out with one red line. You feel it like a missed step. {npc} closes the page gently.

events.text: Far has a price. Every place you sign above the clouds wants you back, and the register cannot pay them all. The Bell Tower has stopped ringing for anyone else. {npc} shows you the slip: [The bell is waiting for one signature only.] "You have made it lonely," {he} says. "Places can be lonely too, up here."

choices.text: Go back and sign the bell tower

effects.log: You go back. The bell rings once, and then, the next morning, for the immortal after you. {npc} marks it in the register: released.
You keep moving. Behind you the bell is silent for a long time. Far is a road; roads leave things behind.

events.text: Ding! Every place above the clouds is signed. The register opens on its own to a page with no dates, only places: the road, the sect gate, a cell, the foot of the Last Door, the Jade Stairs, the bell, the ford. All of them in your hand. {npc} lays a brush beside it. "The Last Calendar," {he} says. "Sign the page itself."

effects.log: You sign the page. Every place on it rings at once, below and above, a bell you hear in your bones. Ding! Ding! Ding!

choices.text: Ask {npc} to sign it with you

effects.log: {npc} hesitates, then signs below your name. An archivist has never signed a register before. The page glows twice as long.

events.text: In the Hall of Heaven's Register the gods sign in like everyone else, and grumble about it. Every place you ever signed is written into one page with no dates, and the page is on the high desk waiting. {npc} has climbed all the way here to stand beside you. "The Last Calendar," {he} whispers. "Even the gods have never finished one."

effects.log: You sign it in front of every god in the hall. Nobody grumbles. Ding! The register shows your name above theirs, for one morning.

choices.text: Sign it quietly, at closing time

effects.log: You wait until the hall is empty and sign it in the lamplight with {npc} holding the lamp. It is the best signature you ever made.

events.text: {npc} comes to the Jade Stairs on the anniversary of your Last Calendar with a slip from the register. "It asks me to tell you," {he} says, "that there is one signature left. You could sign yourself into the register as a place. The next ones would sign in at you. Your ground would be faithful forever." {He} puts the slip away. "I only carry its messages."

effects.log: "Not yet," you say. {npc} looks relieved, and then embarrassed to look relieved.
"I would keep signing," says {npc}. "But I am an archivist. We never know how to end things."

events.text: The register's last message comes by itself, written in the morning frost on the Ford's stepping stones: [One signature left. Sign, and close the book.] {npc} reads it over your shoulder. "For a far one," {he} says, "the last place is the end of the road. I never thought I would see a register say it."

effects.log: You let the frost melt. The message goes with it. It will come back when you want it to.
You copy it into your sleeve, in case. {npc} pretends not to see.

events.text: Ding! Sect goal: none. The System has run out of goals for a sect below, and for the first time it sounds uncertain. Then it draws a plan in the air: four pillars, a roof, a stair of light. [The Cloud Hall.] That same year a young immortal finds you on the isles, dusty from the climb: {npc}, who says {he} learned your forms from a disciple of a disciple of yours, below.

choices.text: Take {him} as the hall's first disciple

effects.log: {npc} kneels on the bare isle where the hall will stand. "Then I am the first," {he} says, "of whatever this becomes."
{npc} shows you the opening form. It is your own, worn smooth by four generations of teachers. You correct one hand. {He} weeps.

events.text: A young immortal waits for you on the isles with an old tablet wrapped in silk: {npc}. "It was in the founder's hall of a sect below," {he} says, "a sect that says it was founded twice, once below and once above, by the same soul." The name on the tablet is not yours. The hand that carved it is. The System says, very quietly: [Welcome back, Sect Lord.]

choices.text: Set the tablet on the isle

effects.log: You set it where the hall will stand. {npc} bows to it, then to you, and does not ask why the hands match.

choices.text: Ask what became of that sect

effects.log: "It is still there," says {npc}. "They light a lamp for its founder every night. They said you would understand."

events.text: The Cloud Hall's plan has a gate in it, and the System wants an answer for the gate: [Open or closed?] Open, and any mortal of your sect who can climb the stair may come up. Closed, and only those you choose. {npc} says: "An immortal sect with mortals climbing into it every few years? The Jade Void will laugh."

choices.text: Open: whoever can climb may come

effects.log: "Let them laugh," you say. The System draws the gate wide. {npc} grins like a disciple who has just been told the sect will feed everyone.
The System draws the gate narrow. "Wise," says {npc}, a little too quickly, and you remember {he} climbed it uninvited.

events.text: An elder of the Jade Void Sect visits your isle to look at the plan, and laughs at it. "A mortal sect, above the clouds? Your disciples will drag the world below up the stairs with them: their quarrels, their debts." {npc}, beside you, has gone red to the ears.

choices.text: Say the world below is welcome

effects.log: "Then let it come," you say. The elder leaves still laughing, but more quietly. {npc} looks at you as if you had built the hall already.

choices.text: Say only the worthy will come

effects.log: "Only the worthy," you say. The elder nods, satisfied. {npc} says nothing, and that evening practises alone a long time.

events.text: The open gate brings them: a disciple of yours from below, then two, then a mortal cook who climbed the stair because the food smelled good. The Cloud Hall is loud now. {npc} brings you the ledger: the immortals of the isles have stopped trading with a sect that lets mortals in.

effects.log: You open the System's strongbox and feed everyone. The cook becomes the most important person on the isle. {npc} learns to chop vegetables.
The cook goes back down the stair, offended. The hall is quieter. {npc} says the soup is worse now, and is right.

events.text: The closed gate keeps the hall quiet and strong, and {npc} unhappy. One night you find out why: {he} has been letting a disciple from below climb the stair at night, a friend of {his} from the old sect, who could never pass your test. "Punish me," {he} says. "Not my friend."

effects.log: You let the friend stay, and give {npc} the key to the gate. "Open it when it should be opened," you say. {He} keeps it on a string at {his} neck.

choices.text: Send the friend back, and forgive {npc}

effects.log: The friend goes back down. {npc} bows and says nothing. The hall stays strong. Something in it does not.

events.text: Ding! Sect goal: The Heavenly Sect Above. The Cloud Hall is a sect now: halls on three isles, a stair of light busy every season, disciples of four generations who call each other brother and sister without asking which world they were born in. {npc} brings the System's last question to you: [Who leads it after you?]

choices.text: Name {npc} as heir of the Cloud Hall

effects.log: {npc} cannot speak for a while. Then {he} says the oath, both versions, the old sect's and the new one. The System records both.
"The sect will choose," you say. The System, for the first time, has no goal to offer. It sounds proud of that.

events.text: In the Divine Realm the gods have sects of their own, and none of them has a stair down to the world of mortals. Yours does. A god of war comes to look at it, and then a god of harvests, and then, quietly, a god nobody prays to any more, who asks to be allowed to sweep the steps. {npc} looks at you: the System's last question waits. [Who leads it after you?]

choices.text: Let the forgotten god sweep, and name {npc} heir

effects.log: The forgotten god sweeps the steps every morning. {npc} becomes heir. The System records a sect of mortals, immortals and one god.
The god weeps, which gods never do. {npc} laughs and hands over the broom. The System has never recorded anything like it.

events.text: The Cloud Hall is old enough now to have its own stories about you, most of them wrong. {npc} comes to the founder's hall at night and finds you staring at the empty altar. "Below," {he} says, "they light a lamp for a founder who is gone. Above, nobody has ever needed to." {He} does not say the rest. {He} does not have to.

choices.text: Say the altar can stay empty a while

effects.log: "A while," you say. {npc} nods, and leaves the lamp unlit, and sits with you until morning.

choices.text: Ask the disciples what they would want

effects.log: The disciples are asked. They want you. They also want, very much, to light a lamp one day. Both, they say. Both is fine.

events.text: The closed gate is still closed, and the hall is the strongest sect on the isles. {npc} keeps the key at {his} neck. One night {he} asks: "When you are a lamp on the altar, may I open it?" It is the only time {npc} has ever asked you for anything.

effects.log: "Yes," you say. {npc} touches the key, and nods, and does not cry until {he} has left the hall.

choices.text: Say it will be {his} hall to decide

effects.log: "It will be yours," you say. {npc} bows very low. In the morning the key is on a better string.

events.text: Ding. The Martial God's Mirror wakes above the clouds like a starving scholar in a library: every immortal you pass is an art it has never seen. On a cloud terrace an immortal in white is practising alone, and the Mirror goes still. "I know that stillness," says the immortal without turning. "{npc}. I carried that Mirror before you. I broke mine."

effects.log: "Because it never copied the one thing worth copying," says {npc}. "Ask it what that is. It will not answer you either."
The Mirror drinks in the form before {npc} finishes the sentence. {He} sighs. "Of course," {he} says. "Of course it does."

events.text: On a cloud terrace an immortal in white stops practising when you arrive. "{npc}," {he} says. "The Mirror's host before you. And before that, you were the host after me, in another life. You copied the Martial God's Last Form. I watched." The Mirror behind your eyes shows you something it has never shown you before: itself, full.

choices.text: Ask what you did with it

effects.log: "You put it down," says {npc}. "Nobody puts it down." {He} looks at you as if you were a riddle {he} solved once and forgot.
You bow to the host before you. {npc} bows back, lower. The Mirror, for once, copies nothing.

events.text: {npc} offers you a bargain on the terrace. "Two arts of the isles. I will show you one. The Cloud-Severing Sword, openly, if you swear to give back what you copy one day. Or you can steal the other, the Palm of the Still Heaven, from the old palm master who teaches it at dawn. The Mirror can do either. You decide what kind of host you are."

effects.log: You swear. {npc} draws, and the sword cuts the clouds in two. The Mirror watches with you, honestly, for once.
At dawn you watch from behind a pillar. The old master's palm stops the wind. The Mirror takes it in silence.

events.text: An immortal of the Jade Void Sect accuses you before the isles' elders: a mortal Mirror, stealing the arts of Heaven. {npc} is asked to judge, as the only one who ever carried one. {He} looks at you a long time. "Show them," {he} says, "or hide it. Either way the Mirror will be watching their swords while they decide."

effects.log: You let the elders see the Mirror. They draw their swords to frighten you, and the Mirror copies the cleanest of them. Honest theft, {npc} calls it.
You lie well. The elders believe you, and in the hall afterwards the palm master stands very still to bless the meeting. The Mirror takes that too.

events.text: A sworn host keeps the oath. {npc} draws again on the terrace, slower this time, so the Mirror can see where the cut begins. "Copy it whole," {he} says, "and then remember you promised it back." It is the first time in your life a master has shown the Mirror an art on purpose.

effects.log: You watch every stroke. The Mirror takes the sword whole, and something else with it: the way {npc} breathes before the cut.

choices.text: Ask to cross swords with it

ok.log: You cross swords. The copy holds against the original. {npc} laughs out loud for the first time in a thousand years.

fail.log: The original cuts the copy in half, gently. You are on the clouds, unhurt, and the Mirror has seen it again anyway.

events.text: The old palm master finds you at dawn behind the same pillar. "Twice," the master says. "The Mirror needs to see it twice, does it not?" It is {npc} behind the palm master, with a face like stone. "I told the master," {npc} says. "I carried a Mirror. I know what it needs."

choices.text: Ask the master to show it once more

effects.log: The palm master is quiet, and then shows it, once, slowly, the way a grandparent shows a child. The Mirror takes it. You feel like a thief anyway.

choices.text: Take it by force of watching

effects.log: You do not ask. The master strikes, to drive you off, and the Mirror takes the palm from the strike itself. {npc} turns away.

events.text: Ding. The Mirror holds the arts of the isles now, and it shows you what it has always wanted: a form it has never seen, because nobody living knows it. The Martial God's Last Form. "It was never a technique," says {npc}, beside you. "It was the god looking at itself in the first mirror. The Mirror wants to look at you the same way."

effects.log: You look into the Mirror and it looks into you, and between the two of you, out of nothing, the Last Form is copied. It is the simplest thing you ever learned.
{npc} stands beside you, and the Mirror sees two hosts at once. The Last Form comes out of the glass like breath.

events.text: In the Divine Realm there is a temple to the Martial God with no statue in it, only a round bronze mirror on the altar. The Mirror behind your eyes and the mirror on the altar see each other, and for a moment you are standing between two infinite halls. {npc}, at the door, will not come in. "This is where I broke mine," {he} says.

choices.text: Stand there until it is copied

effects.log: You stand there a day and a night. Then the infinite halls fold into one form, and the form is in you. {npc} is still at the door.
{npc} comes in. The two mirrors see two hosts, one whole and one broken, and copy the Last Form into both. {He} sits down on the floor and laughs.

events.text: {npc} comes to the terrace on the anniversary of the Last Form. "You swore to give back what you copied," {he} says. "There is one way. Let the Mirror copy its last thing: you. Then you are the art, and anyone who looks into still water can learn it. That is giving back." {He} does not ask you to. {He} only says it exists.

effects.log: "Not yet," you say. {npc} nods. "Neither did I," {he} says. "And then I broke it instead."
You teach it to {npc}, openly, the way {he} taught you the sword. It is the first art you ever gave back.

events.text: The Mirror is full, and does not know what to do with fullness. At night it shows you your own face, over and over, as if practising. {npc} sees it once, reflected in your eyes, and goes pale. "It wants its last copy," {he} says. "You. Then it will shut, and steal nothing ever again. Mine never got that far."

effects.log: The Mirror waits. It practises your face every night anyway, getting it right.
{npc} keeps watch on the terrace for a month. Nothing happens. On the last night {he} says: "When you decide, tell me first."

events.text: Ding! [HIDDEN QUEST LINE UNLOCKED: THE FINAL LEVEL.] A blue window opens above the clouds that is not like the others: it has no close button. On the next cloud an immortal is staring at nothing, the way you stare at your windows. "Level ninety-nine," says {npc}, without turning. "I stopped there. You have the same windows. I can tell by the way you blink."

effects.log: You trade levels, classes, dailies. {npc} laughs at your skill tree and then, quietly, copies one of your choices.
"Because the last level has no level after it," says {npc}. "I was afraid of what that means. You will be too."

events.text: Ding! [WELCOME BACK.] The window says it to you above the clouds, and nothing else, for a whole day. Then an immortal on the next cloud waves. "{npc}," {he} says. "You do not remember me. In another life you advanced your class right there and the whole sky turned blue for a second. I have been waiting for it to happen again."

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It does not matter, the window says, you may choose again. {npc} looks almost jealous.

choices.text: Say you will try to make the sky blue again

effects.log: "Do it on a clear day," says {npc}. "The view is better."

events.text: [QUEST: CHOOSE A PLAYSTYLE FOR THE FINAL LEVEL.] Two buttons: [CLEAR] and [PLAY]. {npc} explains: "Clear is speed. Every daily, every efficient kill, straight to the top. Play is the side quests: the people, the places, the things the System pays nothing for. I picked clear. That is why I stopped at ninety-nine."

effects.log: [PLAYSTYLE: CLEAR.] The windows sharpen. Your experience bar moves faster. {npc} nods as if watching an old mistake made more cleverly.
[PLAYSTYLE: PLAY.] The windows soften. A side quest appears at once: help {npc} with something {he} never finished.

events.text: A window opens over {npc}'s head, which should be impossible: you can only see your own. [PARTY INVITE: ACCEPT?] {npc} sees it too, in reverse. "I have never been in a party," {he} says. "I solo-cleared everything. It was very efficient and very lonely."

choices.text: Decline: the final level is solo

effects.log: [PARTY DECLINED.] {npc} nods. "Correct," {he} says, and sounds sad about being correct.
[PARTY FORMED: 2 MEMBERS.] {npc} stares at the little number two for a long time.

events.text: [DAILY QUESTS: 300 OF 300 COMPLETE.] Clear works. Your bar is racing toward the top, and the windows have stopped saying anything except numbers. {npc} finds you grinding the same isle's spirit beasts for the ninth year running. "This is the part where I stopped feeling anything," {he} says. "Just so you know where it is."

choices.text: Stop and look at the view

effects.log: You stop. The isle is beautiful. You never noticed, because it was a farming spot. [NO EXPERIENCE GAINED.] You do not care.
You keep going. [LEVEL UP.] [LEVEL UP.] The windows are very pleased with you. You are not sure you are.

events.text: [SIDE QUEST: THE THING {npc} NEVER FINISHED.] It turns out to be a letter. To a friend from the world below, written at level twelve, never sent, now nine hundred years late. "The friend is dead," {npc} says. "The quest is still open. The System never closes a side quest."

choices.text: Deliver it to the friend's grave below

effects.log: You climb down the white stairs and leave the letter on a grave nobody tends. [SIDE QUEST COMPLETE.] {npc} does not stop crying for a day.

choices.text: Help {him} write a new one, to the friend's line

effects.log: You write it together, to a great-great-grandchild. The reply comes a year later, in a child's hand. [SIDE QUEST COMPLETE, BONUS.] The bonus is the letter.

events.text: Ding! [LEVEL 40: CLASS ADVANCEMENT QUEST.] The blue window that never closes opens fully. Behind it is a stair of light, and at the top a door, and on the door three classes drawn as stances, no words. {npc} stands beside you at the foot of it. "I never climbed it," {he} says. "Ninety-nine levels, and I never climbed it."

effects.log: You climb. At the door the window says [CHOOSE], and waits. You will choose in the ledger, when you are ready. {npc} watched the whole climb.
[PARTY CLASS ADVANCEMENT.] The stair is wide enough for two. At the top {npc} stops at the door and lets you go first. "Next time," {he} says.

events.text: In the Divine Realm even the gods have no windows. Yours open here anyway, and the gods stop to stare at the blue light. [CLASS ADVANCEMENT QUEST.] A stair of light goes up from the Hall of Heaven's Register to a door in the sky. {npc} has climbed all the way up to the Divine Realm just to see you do it.

choices.text: Climb it in front of the gods

effects.log: You climb while the gods watch. At the door the window says [CHOOSE]. A god asks {npc} what level you are. {npc} says: "Enough."
You climb at night. At the door the window says [CHOOSE], and then, smaller: [WELL DONE.] You did not know it could say that.

events.text: The windows are quieter since the class advancement. One last quest sits at the bottom of the list, greyed, never offered: [THE FINAL LEVEL: ENTER?] {npc} sees you looking at it. "Clear players always end up here," {he} says. "At the last button. If you press it, the game is cleared. I do not know what cleared means. Nobody who knows has come back."

effects.log: You leave it. The quest stays at the bottom of the list, patient as a door.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to tell you if {he} ever presses it

effects.log: "You first," says {npc}, and then, quickly, "I mean, I will tell you. Of course I will."

events.text: [PARTY: 2 MEMBERS.] The little number two has been in the corner of your windows for years now. One evening a quest appears for both of you: [THE FINAL LEVEL: ENTER?], greyed. {npc} laughs. "It waited for a party," {he} says. "Of course it did. It is a terrible game designer and a good friend."

effects.log: "Not yet," you say. {npc} nods. "Not yet is a good answer," {he} says. "It is the one I never had."
You do the dailies together. They are very small quests. You laugh at them the whole way.

events.text: [The eight stars are restless.] Above the clouds they are close enough to hear muttering. And between them, where the stargazers' charts have always left a gap, there is a darkness that is listening too. An immortal in dark robes at a bronze sphere notices you noticing it. "{npc}, of the Bright Hall," {he} says. "Nobody else looks at the empty place. Sit."

effects.log: {npc} shows you a thousand years of charts. The gap is on every one of them, and on the oldest someone has written: "Not empty. Waiting."

choices.text: Ask what your sponsor thinks of the gap

effects.log: [Your sponsor] goes quiet. The other seven laugh nervously. "Even stars are afraid of something," says {npc}.

events.text: The stargazer {npc} has a chart with your name on it, drawn in another life: a line from the empty place among the eight down to a little cross that is you. "It chose someone once," {he} says, "and the eight have been nervous about it ever since. The cross was in the same place as your feet."

choices.text: Ask {him} to draw a new line

effects.log: {npc} draws a faint new line from the gap to where you stand now. Above you, the darkness between the stars feels a little closer.

choices.text: Say you do not want to be chosen twice

effects.log: "Nobody wants it," says {npc}. "That is usually why it chooses them."

events.text: [The Constellations are bidding.] Now that the ninth has noticed you, the other seven want you too, and say so: coins, gifts, little messages at night. Your sponsor sulks. {npc} watches the sky. "The ninth chooses by watching what you do with the eight," {he} says. "Stay true to one, or play to all. I have never seen which it likes."

effects.log: [Your sponsor is moved.] The other seven go quiet, a little offended. {npc} marks the chart: "Loyal."
[The eight are entertained.] Coins rain down from every side. Your sponsor sulks for a decade. {npc} marks the chart: "A story for everyone."

events.text: A star falls on the isles: one of the minor ones, a messenger, burned out from carrying too many bids to you. {npc} kneels by the cooling stone. "They are fighting over you," {he} says, "and the little lights pay for it. The ninth is watching what you do about that."

choices.text: Tell your sponsor to stop the bidding

effects.log: [Your sponsor obeys you.] It is the first time a star has obeyed anyone. The bids stop. {npc} buries the messenger's stone.

choices.text: Tell all eight: one story, for all of them

effects.log: The eight agree, grudgingly, to share you. The bids become applause instead. {npc} keeps the stone on the sphere.

events.text: Loyalty has a price. The other seven have decided your story is boring, and say so, loudly, every night. Your sponsor is fiercely happy and very lonely. {npc} brings you a chart showing the eight drifting apart, your sponsor alone on one side of the sky. "A loyal star is a star with no friends," {he} says.

choices.text: Find your sponsor a friend among the eight

effects.log: You do a thing the seventh star loves, for your sponsor. [Your sponsor and another star nod to each other.] {npc} redraws the chart.
[Your sponsor is moved.] The two of you, a star and a soul, against seven. {npc} draws a single bright line.

events.text: Playing to all eight has a price. Every scene of your life is a performance now, and you catch yourself choosing what the stars like instead of what you want. {npc} catches you at it too. "The eight are an audience," {he} says. "The ninth is not. The ninth looks for whoever is left when the audience goes home."

choices.text: Do one thing none of the stars would like

effects.log: You do one small, kind, boring thing. [No star reacts.] It is the best day you have had in years. The darkness between the stars seems to lean closer.
[The eight laugh, weep and applaud.] Coins everywhere. {npc} looks away, and you do not like how that feels.

events.text: The darkness between the stars opens one eye. [The Last Star] has not risen. It does not need to. It has been watching your story since before you were born, and it says only: [I choose you.] The eight go perfectly silent. {npc} has dropped the chart and does not pick it up.

effects.log: [The Last Star has chosen you.] The silence of the eight becomes a different thing: respect. {npc} writes, with a shaking hand, a new star on the chart.
[Because you looked back.] That is all it says. {npc} laughs, once. "Stargazers," {he} says. "We were the only ones who ever did."

events.text: In the Divine Realm the stars are not lights: they are gods, and the eight are here in person, uncomfortable in robes. The ninth chair at their table has always been empty. Tonight a voice comes from it, though nobody sits there: [I choose this one.] {npc}, who climbed all the way up to see the eight with {his} own eyes, sits down on the floor.

effects.log: You sit in the ninth chair. The eight bow, all of them, even the Lantern Who Burns for Others. {npc} is crying and drawing at the same time.

choices.text: Pull up a chair for {npc} too

effects.log: You pull a tenth chair to the table for {npc}. The eight stare. The ninth voice laughs, which nobody knew it could.

events.text: Your sponsor and the Last Star both watch over you now, which your sponsor finds very stressful. One night the Last Star speaks again: [You could rise.] Become the ninth star. Shine beside the one that sponsored you, and watch the stories below. {npc} hears it, as stargazers hear everything. "I would chart you," {he} says quietly. "Every night."

effects.log: "Not yet," you say. [Your sponsor sighs with relief.] {npc} pretends to adjust the sphere.

choices.text: Ask your sponsor what it wants

effects.log: [Your sponsor wants you to be happy.] It is the least starlike thing a star has ever said. {npc} writes it down.

events.text: The eight still applaud your story, but softer now, the way an audience does near the end. The Last Star says: [You could rise, and watch with kinder eyes than theirs.] {npc}, at the sphere, has already drawn a place for you on tomorrow's chart, in pencil. "Just in case," {he} says. "Pencil rubs out."

effects.log: You leave it. Every night {npc} draws it again, very lightly, and every morning it is still there.
You rub it out. "Not yet," you say. {npc} nods and puts the pencil behind {his} ear, where it stays.
